name: Persian Beef Koobideh (Skillet)
ingredients:
1 kg ground beef (70/30 lean/fat)
1 large brown onion
1 large egg
1 tbsp kosher salt
1 1/2 tsp ground turmeric
1/2 tsp ground black pepper
1 tbsp saffron water
2 tbsp beef tallow
3-4 garlic cloves, crushed
directions:
1. Grate the onion finely. Keep the juice - no need to squeeze it out for skillet patties.
2. In a bowl, combine the grated onion with salt, turmeric, black pepper, saffron water, and egg. Whisk to combine.
3. Add the beef. Knead with your hands for 2-3 minutes until uniform and slightly tacky so the patties hold together.
4. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes (up to 2 hours for deeper flavor).
5. Heat beef tallow in a skillet over high heat until shimmering.
6. Form the meat into balls and place in the hot skillet, pressing each flat with a spatula.
7. Cook 3 minutes on the first side.
8. Flip, reduce the heat slightly, and drop in the crushed garlic cloves.
9. Baste the patties in the pan juices for another 4-5 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 140°F.
10. Serve immediately with chelo, grilled tomato, sumac, and fresh herbs.
notes:
Saffron water: grind 1/4 tsp saffron threads with a pinch of salt in a mortar. Steep in 3 tbsp hot (not boiling) water for 10+ min. Keeps refrigerated 1 week.

70/30 fat ratio keeps the patties juicy and gives you plenty of pan juices for basting.
